source_scope.ag_thermodynamics: The user-provided summary attributes Ag heat capacity, melting point, latent heat, and density anchors to NIST/CDC thermophysical tables.
source_scope.ag_thermal_conductivity: The user-provided summary attributes solid and liquid conductivity anchors to NIST recommended data; the liquid value is described there as tentative.
source_scope.ti3sic2: The 300 K and 1473.15 K Ti3SiC2 anchors are attributed to Barsoum et al.; the 2000 K row is an explicit linear extrapolation of the existing anchor trends, not a measured value. Son et al. (2016) provides first-principles finite-temperature context through 1400 K, not a 2000 K data point.
source_scope.provenance_limit: The exact bibliographic records and source tables are not yet archived in this checkout. These values are implementation candidates pending source-table attachment and citation audit.

ag.thermal_density_policy: Use fixed solid reference density for the first enthalpy-volume solver; do not claim thermal expansion or liquid-volume change is modeled.
ag.solid_cp_interpolation: Piecewise linear in temperature through thermophysical_candidates.csv anchors at 300 K and Tm.
ag.liquid_cp_interpolation: Constant at the single supplied melting-point anchor; no temperature trend is inferred.
ag.solid_conductivity_interpolation: Piecewise linear between 300 K and Tm anchors.
ag.liquid_conductivity_interpolation: Constant at the single supplied melting-point anchor; tentative source status remains attached.

ti3sic2.heat_capacity_interpolation: Linear continuation of the existing 300 K to 1473.15 K candidate slope through the 2000 K extrapolated anchor; the 2000 K value is a model assumption, not a measurement.
ti3sic2.conductivity_interpolation: Linear continuation of the existing 300 K to 1473.15 K candidate slope through the 2000 K extrapolated anchor; the 2000 K value is a model assumption, not a measurement.

high_temperature_extension.method: Continue the original two-anchor linear Cp and k trends without changing their slopes.

specific_heat_conversion_check_J_kg_K.note: Corrected by dividing by Ti3SiC2 formula molar mass 195.708 g/mol; the 656–924 J/(kg K) conversion in the supplied summary is inconsistent with this formula mass.

source.note: The conversion uses 1 eV = 1.602176634e-19 J, 1 ps = 1e-12 s, and 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m. Source power remains weighted by Ag volume fraction and is not renormalized after masking.

boundary_cases.A: Adiabatic scaffold: no heat flux through the Ag/skeleton boundary; pure geometric confinement baseline.
boundary_cases.B: Ideal thermal contact: shared temperature and continuous heat flux with a dynamically conducting and heat-storing Ti3SiC2 phase; zero added interface resistance.

extrapolation_policy: Stop if Ti3SiC2 exceeds 2000 K. The 1473.15–2000 K Cp and conductivity values are explicit linear continuations of the previous candidate trends, not experimentally validated high-temperature data. Ag solid anchors are restricted to 300 K through Tm; liquid Cp and conductivity are constant single-anchor assumptions, not sourced temperature curves.
